393	    def enforce_ex(self, *rvals):
   394	        """decides whether a "subject" can access a "object" with the operation "action",
   395	        input parameters are usually: (sub, obj, act).
   396	        return judge result with reason
   397	        """
   398	
   399	        rtype = "r"
   400	        ptype = "p"
   401	        etype = "e"
   402	        mtype = "m"
   403	
   404	        if not self.enabled:
   405	            return [True, []]
   406	
   407	        functions = self.fm.get_functions()
   408	
   409	        if "g" in self.model.keys():
   410	            for key, ast in self.model["g"].items():
   411	                if len(self.rm_map) != 0:
   412	                    functions[key] = generate_g_function(ast.rm)
   413	                if len(self.cond_rm_map) != 0:
   414	                    functions[key] = generate_conditional_g_function(ast.cond_rm)
   415	
   416	        if len(rvals) != 0:
   417	            if isinstance(rvals[0], EnforceContext):
   418	                enforce_context = rvals[0]
   419	                rtype = enforce_context.rtype
   420	                ptype = enforce_context.ptype
   421	                etype = enforce_context.etype
   422	                mtype = enforce_context.mtype
   423	                rvals = rvals[1:]
   424	
   425	        if "m" not in self.model.keys():
   426	            raise RuntimeError("model is undefined")
   427	
   428	        if "m" not in self.model["m"].keys():
   429	            raise RuntimeError("model is undefined")
   430	
   431	        r_tokens = self.model["r"][rtype].tokens
   432	        p_tokens = self.model["p"][ptype].tokens
   433	
   434	        if len(r_tokens) != len(rvals):
   435	            raise RuntimeError("invalid request size")
   436	
   437	        exp_string = self.model["m"][mtype].value
   438	        exp_has_eval = util.has_eval(exp_string)
   439	        if not exp_has_eval:
   440	            expression = self._get_expression(exp_string, functions)
   441	
   442	        policy_effects = set()
   443	
   444	        r_parameters = dict(zip(r_tokens, rvals))
   445	
   446	        policy_len = len(self.model["p"][ptype].policy)
   447	
   448	        explain_index = -1
   449	        if not 0 == policy_len:
   450	            for i, pvals in enumerate(self.model["p"][ptype].policy):
   451	                if len(p_tokens) != len(pvals):
   452	                    raise RuntimeError("invalid policy size")
   453	
   454	                p_parameters = dict(zip(p_tokens, pvals))
   455	                parameters = dict(r_parameters, **p_parameters)
   456	
   457	                if exp_has_eval:
   458	                    rule_names = util.get_eval_value(exp_string)
   459	                    rules = [util.escape_assertion(p_parameters[rule_name]) for rule_name in rule_names]
   460	                    exp_with_rule = util.replace_eval(exp_string, rules)
   461	                    expression = self._get_expression(exp_with_rule, functions)
   462	
   463	                result = expression.eval(parameters)
   464	
   465	                if isinstance(result, bool):
   466	                    if not result:
   467	                        policy_effects.add(Effector.INDETERMINATE)
   468	                        continue
   469	                elif isinstance(result, float):
   470	                    if 0 == result:
   471	                        policy_effects.add(Effector.INDETERMINATE)
   472	                        continue
   473	                else:
   474	                    raise RuntimeError("matcher result should be bool, int or float")
   475	
   476	                p_eft_key = ptype + "_eft"
   477	                if p_eft_key in parameters.keys():
   478	                    eft = parameters[p_eft_key]
   479	                    if "allow" == eft:
   480	                        policy_effects.add(Effector.ALLOW)
   481	                    elif "deny" == eft:
   482	                        policy_effects.add(Effector.DENY)
   483	                    else:
   484	                        policy_effects.add(Effector.INDETERMINATE)
   485	                else:
   486	                    policy_effects.add(Effector.ALLOW)
   487	
   488	                # Update explain_index for any matching policy before checking early break condition
   489	                # to ensure explanations are captured for allow rules in deny models
   490	                explain_index = i
   491	
   492	                if self.eft.intermediate_effect(policy_effects) != Effector.INDETERMINATE:
   493	                    break
   494	
   495	        else:
   496	            if exp_has_eval:
   497	                raise RuntimeError("please make sure rule exists in policy when using eval() in matcher")
   498	
   499	            parameters = r_parameters.copy()
   500	
   501	            for token in self.model["p"][ptype].tokens:
   502	                parameters[token] = ""
   503	
   504	            result = expression.eval(parameters)
   505	
   506	            if result:
   507	                policy_effects.add(Effector.ALLOW)
   508	            else:
   509	                policy_effects.add(Effector.INDETERMINATE)
   510	
   511	        final_effect = self.eft.final_effect(policy_effects)
   512	        result = effect_to_bool(final_effect)
   513	
   514	        # Log request.
   515	        if (result and self.logger.isEnabledFor(logging.INFO)) or (
   516	            not result and self.logger.isEnabledFor(logging.WARNING)
   517	        ):
   518	            req_str = "Request: "
   519	            req_str = req_str + ", ".join([str(v) for v in rvals])
   520	            req_str = req_str + " ---> %s" % result
   521	            if result:
   522	                self.logger.info(req_str)
   523	            else:
   524	                # leaving this in warning for now, if it's very noise this can be changed to info or debug,
   525	                # or change the log level
   526	                self.logger.warning(req_str)
   527	
   528	        explain_rule = []
   529	        if explain_index != -1 and explain_index < policy_len:
   530	            explain_rule = self.model["p"][ptype].policy[explain_index]
   531	
   532	        return result, explain_rule

   537	        for request in rvals:

   539	            results.append(result)

   114	    def __deepcopy__(self, memo):
   115	        """Custom deepcopy implementation that copies policy data only,
   116	        sharing rm and cond_rm by reference instead of cloning them.
   117	
   118	        The role managers are live, shared, cyclic object graphs: deep-copying them
   119	        races with concurrent add_link() calls from another thread (as happens when a
   120	        watcher reloads the policy), and the copy is discarded by build_role_links()
   121	        anyway. This matches casbin-go, whose Assertion.copy() also carries RM and
   122	        CondRM over by reference.
   123	        """
   124	        cls = self.__class__
   125	        result = cls.__new__(cls)
   126	        memo[id(self)] = result
   127	        for k, v in self.__dict__.items():
   128	            if k in ("rm", "cond_rm"):
   129	                setattr(result, k, v)
   130	            else:
   131	                setattr(result, k, copy.deepcopy(v, memo))
   132	        return result

   166	    def get_subject_hierarchy_map(self, policies):
   167	        """
   168	        Get the subject hierarchy from the policy.
   169	        Select the lowest level subject in multiple rounds until all subjects are selected.
   170	        Return the subject hierarchy dictionary, the subject is the key, and the level is the value.
   171	        The level starts from 0 and increases in turn. The smaller the level, the higher the priority.
   172	        """
   173	        # Init unsorted policy, and subject
   174	        unsorted_policy = []
   175	        unsorted_sub = set()
   176	        for policy in policies:
   177	            if len(policy) < 2:
   178	                raise RuntimeError("policy g expect 2 more params")
   179	            domain = DEFAULT_DOMAIN
   180	            if len(policy) != 2:
   181	                domain = policy[2]
   182	            child = self.get_name_with_domain(domain, policy[0])
   183	            parent = self.get_name_with_domain(domain, policy[1])
   184	            unsorted_policy.append([child, parent])
   185	            unsorted_sub.add(child)
   186	            unsorted_sub.add(parent)
   187	        # sort policy,and update sorted_sub_list
   188	        sorted_sub_list = []
   189	        while len(unsorted_policy) > 0:
   190	            # get all parent subject
   191	            parent_sub = {p[1] for p in unsorted_policy if p[1] != ""}
   192	            # remove parent subject from unsorted_sub
   193	            sorted_sub = unsorted_sub - parent_sub
   194	            if not sorted_sub:
   195	                raise RuntimeError("cycle dependency in subject hierarchy.subjects: {}".format(unsorted_sub))
   196	            # update sorted_sub_list
   197	            sorted_sub_list.append(sorted_sub)
   198	            # remove sorted subject, and update unsorted_policy
   199	            unsorted_policy = [p for p in unsorted_policy if p[0] not in sorted_sub]
   200	            # update unsorted_sub
   201	            unsorted_sub = unsorted_sub - sorted_sub
   202	        if len(unsorted_sub) > 0:
   203	            sorted_sub_list.append(unsorted_sub)
   204	        # Tree structure of subject
   205	        return {sub: i for i, subs in enumerate(sorted_sub_list) for sub in subs}

    38	class _DeferredNotifier:
    39	    """Queues the watcher notifications raised inside a locked section and delivers them
    40	    once the lock has been released.
    41	
    42	    Watchers have a lock of their own, and some of them (the redis watcher, for one) hold
    43	    it while running the update callback, which calls back into the enforcer to reload the
    44	    policy. Notifying from inside the enforcer lock would let the two threads take those
    45	    two locks in opposite orders and deadlock:
    46	    https://github.com/casbin/pycasbin/issues/408
    47	    """
    48	
    49	    def __init__(self):
    50	        self._local = threading.local()
    51	
    52	    def _stack(self):
    53	        stack = getattr(self._local, "stack", None)
    54	        if stack is None:
    55	            stack = []
    56	            self._local.stack = stack
    57	        return stack
    58	
    59	    def defer(self, func, args, kwargs):
    60	        """queues a call, and returns whether it was queued. False means no lock is held
    61	        by this thread, so the caller has to run the call itself."""
    62	        stack = self._stack()
    63	        if not stack:
    64	            return False
    65	        stack[-1].append((func, args, kwargs))
    66	        return True
    67	
    68	    def begin(self):
    69	        """starts collecting, called right after the lock has been taken."""
    70	        self._stack().append([])
    71	
    72	    def end(self, suppress_errors=False):
    73	        """delivers what was collected, called right after the lock has been released."""
    74	        stack = self._stack()
    75	        queued = stack.pop()
    76	        if stack:
    77	            # an outer lock is still held, so hand the calls over to it
    78	            stack[-1].extend(queued)
